ai_root_cause: Fa0/2 is on default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10, so PC2 is in a different broadcast domain than PC1.
expected_fault: Fa0/2 was left in default VLAN 1 instead of VLAN 10 (VLAN mismatch on access port).

ai_root_cause: VLAN 20 is not in the trunk's allowed VLAN list on SW1.
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is not in the allowed list on SW1's trunk (switchport trunk allowed vlan misconfigured).

ai_root_cause: Fa0/5 was never assigned to VLAN 30 and remains on default VLAN 1.
expected_fault: Port never had switchport access vlan 30 applied; still default VLAN 1.

ai_root_cause: Sub-interface Gi0/0.30 is administratively down.
expected_fault: Sub-interface for VLAN 30 exists but is administratively down (no 'no shutdown' applied, or missing encapsulation).

ai_root_cause: The IP phone is not receiving power/registering correctly, likely a PoE issue.
expected_fault: Voice VLAN was never configured on the port, so the phone pulled default settings and shares the data VLAN oddly, breaking the PC's trunked path.

ai_root_cause: SW2's VTP configuration revision is stale and needs to be reset.
expected_fault: SW2 never received the VTP update (revision numbers match but VLAN 40 is missing on SW2, indicating the trunk carrying VTP advertisements was down when the change was made).

ai_root_cause: PC1's default gateway (192.168.1.100) does not match R1's interface IP (192.168.1.1).
expected_fault: PC1's configured default gateway (192.168.1.100) does not match the router's actual interface IP (192.168.1.1) - gateway mismatch.

ai_root_cause: The VLAN 10 SVI is administratively down, so it cannot route as the gateway.
expected_fault: SVI (VLAN 10 interface) is administratively shut down, so it cannot act as gateway.

ai_root_cause: ip routing is not enabled globally on the multilayer switch.
expected_fault: 'ip routing' is not enabled globally on the multilayer switch, so it behaves as a pure Layer 2 device and never routes between SVIs.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP relay agent is not configured on the VLAN 30 interface.
expected_fault: DHCP pool is missing the 'default-router' statement, so clients never learn a gateway.

ai_root_cause: Subnet mask mismatch between the server (/25) and the router interface (/24) on the same segment.
expected_fault: Subnet mask mismatch (/25 on host vs /24 on router) causes the host to miscalculate which addresses are local, breaking off-subnet routing decisions.

ai_root_cause: Missing ip helper-address on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the DHCP server.
expected_fault: Missing 'ip helper-address' on the VLAN 40 SVI, so DHCP broadcasts never reach the centralized DHCP server.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 is too small (/28) for the number of hosts, exhausting available addresses.
expected_fault: DHCP pool address space is exhausted (too small a subnet mask for the number of hosts).

ai_root_cause: A duplicate/legacy DHCP pool (TESTPOOL) is overlapping and serving the wrong gateway.
expected_fault: A stale duplicate DHCP pool (TESTPOOL) overlaps the real VLAN20POOL and is being served instead, handing out the wrong gateway.

ai_root_cause: Static printer IP was never excluded from the DHCP pool, causing a duplicate/conflicting lease.
expected_fault: Static IP for the printer (192.168.10.50) was never excluded from the DHCP pool, so the DHCP server also leases it out (duplicate IP).

ai_root_cause: A specific host on VLAN 50 has a firewall blocking DHCP broadcasts.
expected_fault: DHCP service is globally disabled on the router ('no service dhcp'), so no pool responds anywhere, not just VLAN 50.

ai_root_cause: The DNS A record for fileserver.corp.local does not exist on the DNS server.
expected_fault: The A record for fileserver.corp.local does not exist on the DNS server (missing/incorrect DNS zone record), not a connectivity problem.

ai_root_cause: The DHCP pool for VLAN 10 never specifies a dns-server, so clients have no resolver configured.
expected_fault: DHCP pool never specifies a dns-server, so clients have no DNS resolver configured, even though IP connectivity is fine (classic Layer 3 works / Layer 7 fails split).

ai_root_cause: The affected PC's network cable or NIC driver is faulty.
expected_fault: This PC was statically configured to use itself (127.0.0.1) as its DNS server instead of the real DNS server.

ai_root_cause: The internal DNS server has no forwarder configured for external domain queries.
expected_fault: Internal DNS server has no forwarder configured for external queries, so it can answer only internal corp.local records.

ai_root_cause: R1's static route destination network has a typo (192.168.3.0 instead of 192.168.2.0).
expected_fault: Static route on R1 points to the wrong destination network (192.168.3.0 instead of 192.168.2.0) - typo in the route statement.

ai_root_cause: R1 and R2 are configured with mismatched OSPF process IDs, preventing adjacency.
expected_fault: Area mismatch: R1 advertises the link in area 0 while R2 advertises it in area 1, so OSPF adjacency never forms.

ai_root_cause: The static route for 192.168.99.0/24 points to a next-hop IP that is not a real device on that subnet.
expected_fault: Static route for 192.168.99.0/24 points to a next-hop IP (192.168.1.254) that is not a real, reachable device on that subnet.

ai_root_cause: R3, the new transit router, has no routing protocol or static routes configured.
expected_fault: R3, the new transit router, has no routing protocol or static routes configured, so it silently drops traffic destined beyond its directly connected interfaces.

ai_root_cause: A duplex mismatch on one of the equal-cost links is causing CRC errors and intermittent loss.
expected_fault: Duplex mismatch on one of the two equal-cost links causes high CRC/input errors, leading to intermittent packet loss on that path.

ai_root_cause: OSPF adjacency between R1 and R2 has failed due to a hello/dead timer mismatch.
expected_fault: The OSPF area range mask is wrong (/24 instead of the intended /22), so the summary does not cover all the subordinate subnets, and some routes are missing.

ai_root_cause: ACL 101 only permits ICMP to the server and implicitly denies all other traffic, including the TCP ports needed for file/web access.
expected_fault: ACL 101 only permits ICMP to the server and denies everything else, including the TCP ports needed for file sharing/HTTP (Layer 3/4 filtering issue).

ai_root_cause: The GUEST-ACL exists with correct rules but was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface.
expected_fault: The GUEST-ACL access list is correctly written but was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface (ip access-group missing).

ai_root_cause: The ADMIN-ACL access-class is missing from the VTY lines entirely.
expected_fault: The ACL entry has source and destination reversed - it should permit traffic FROM the admin host TO the router, but as written it only matches traffic sourced from port 22, not destined to it.

ai_root_cause: ACL 110 has only a deny statement, so the implicit deny-all at the end blocks all traffic, not just the intended subnet.
expected_fault: ACL 110 has only a deny statement and relies on the implicit 'deny any any' at the end, so it blocks everything instead of just the intended subnet.

ai_root_cause: The inside LAN interface (Gi0/0) is missing 'ip nat inside', so NAT never triggers.
expected_fault: The inside LAN interface (Gi0/0) is missing the 'ip nat inside' command, so NAT never triggers for internal traffic even though the overload statement exists.

ai_root_cause: The ISP link itself is down, so no NAT translations can succeed.
expected_fault: Static NAT rule maps the wrong internal port (8080) while the server listens on 80, so translated connections reach the host on the wrong port and are refused.

ai_root_cause: The NAT overload ACL (ACL 1) does not include the 192.168.50.0/24 network, so it is never translated.
expected_fault: The NAT source ACL (ACL 1) never includes the 192.168.50.0/24 network, so PAT never matches and translates traffic from that subnet.

ai_root_cause: Missing ip helper-address on the VLAN 15 SVI, so wireless DHCP requests never reach the DHCP server.
expected_fault: Same root cause pattern as wired DHCP relay issues: VLAN 15's SVI is missing 'ip helper-address', so wireless DHCP requests never reach the DHCP server.

ai_root_cause: Both APs are on the same channel with overlapping coverage, causing co-channel interference.
expected_fault: Both APs are set to the same channel (6) with overlapping coverage, causing co-channel interference and roaming drops.

ai_root_cause: GUEST-ACL was never applied to the VLAN 60 interface.
expected_fault: The GUEST-ACL is applied correctly to VLAN 60 but its rules were edited to a blanket permit, so it no longer actually restricts guest traffic (security/isolation issue).
